## The Core Systems Tension: Digital Idempotency vs. The Physical Substrate

For decades, computer systems were engineered under the assumption of **digital idempotency**: if an operation fails or encounters an exception, it can be caught in a `try/catch` block, rolled back in a database transaction, or retried across an HTTP network connection without altering the state of the universe.

```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               THE DIGITAL PARADIGM vs. THE PHYSICAL AI PARADIGM                        │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  DIGITAL ML:  Input X ──► [Neural Network] ──► Output Y                                │
│               Exception? ──► [try / catch] ──► Retry (World State W_t Unchanged)       │
│                                                                                        │
│  PHYSICAL AI: Photons / Voltages ──► [Learned Model] ──(Proposal p_t)──┐               │
│                                                                        ▼               │
│               [Actuators / Inverters] ◄──(Permit u_t)── [Real-Time MCU Enforcer]       │
│                         │                                                              │
│                         ▼                                                              │
│               Physical Action A_t ──► Mutates Matter & Energy (W_t ──► W_t+1)          │
│                                                 │                                      │
│                                                 ▼                                      │
│                                       Endogenous Observation O_t+1                     │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**In Physical AI Systems, software moves matter.** The moment an electric motor inverts current, a hydraulic valve opens, or a battery bank discharges, electrical energy transduces into kinetic momentum ($p = mv$) and thermal dissipation ($I^2 R$). By the fundamental laws of classical mechanics and thermodynamics, physical actions cannot be rewound: **you cannot `ctrl+z` kinetic energy.**

Furthermore, the physical universe does not pause while a neural network computes. Sensor data decays the instant it is sampled; stale information ($\Delta t$) degrades control stability; and operating system scheduling jitter can expand physical stopping distances ($d_{\text{stop}}$) beyond safe clearance margins.

Part I establishes the immutable physical, temporal, and runtime foundations that govern every acting machine.

## The Three Bedrock Architectural Pillars of Part I

```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        PART I ARCHITECTURAL SUBSTRATE                                  │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                                        │
│   [Stochastic ML Models / Linux MPU] ──(Untrusted Proposals)──┐                         │
│                                                               │                        │
│   ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╪══════════════════════  │
│   PROPOSAL–PERMISSION BOUNDARY: Multi-Rate IPC & Watchdogs    │ (Chapter 3)            │
│   ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╪══════════════════════  │
│                                                               ▼                        │
│   [Bare-Metal MCU Enforcer] ──► [Power Bus Isolation] ──► [ACTUATORS / MATTER] (Ch 1)  │
│          ▲                              │                                              │
│          └────── Freshness Δt & P99 ────┴────── (Hardware Metrology & Timers) (Ch 2)   │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 1. Physical Causality (Chapter 1)
Drawing the causal boundary separating virtual computation from matter and energy. We establish why stochastic learned models running on application processors must be treated as **untrusted proposal services**, isolate power electronics with hardware emergency loops, formulate the 3-part Causal Boundary criterion across the embodiment spectrum, and freeze the system's **Loop Charter** (`LOOP-01`).

### 2. Time and Latency (Chapter 2)
Measuring the complete sensory-motor path down to the microsecond. We deconstruct latency across photon integration, DMA transfer, inference compute, IPC queues, and coil inductance rise times; model information age ($\Delta t$) and freshness decay; prove why average latency is a dangerous metric compared to tail distributions ($P_{99}, P_{99.9}$); derive dynamic stopping distance physics ($d_{\text{stop}}$); and formalize the **Requirements and Latency Budget Ledger** (`REQ-01`).

### 3. Multi-Rate Systems (Chapter 3)
Bridging the three fundamental speeds of intelligence: $1\text{ Hz}$ semantic deliberation, $20\text{--}50\text{ Hz}$ trajectory planning, and $1000\text{ Hz}$ bare-metal motor reflexes. We architect lock-free shared memory ring buffers across heterogeneous processor domains (Linux MPU $\leftrightarrow$ Cortex-M4 MCU), configure hardware heartbeat watchdog leases ($\tau_{\text{watchdog}}$), and prove on the bench that the real-time core safely halts actuators when the application processor crashes via the **Continuous Runtime Skeleton** (`RUN-01`).

---

## The Bench Reality on the TinyAgent

Throughout Part I, concepts are directly realized and measured on the **TinyAgents Kit (Arduino UNO Q Dual-Brain)**:

* **Hardware Power Isolation:** Wiring the independent actuator power rail through a hardware emergency interlock relay controlled exclusively by the MCU.
* **Sense-to-Actuation Profiler:** Instrumenting GPIO toggles and PTP hardware clocks to capture millisecond latency histograms ($P_{50}, P_{90}, P_{99}$) from camera exposure to motor torque generation.
* **Kernel Panic Survival Trial:** Injecting an unhandled SIGKILL / memory fault into the Linux Python process while the motor is energized at full speed, verifying that the Cortex-M4 MCU watchdog timer trips within $5\text{ ms}$ and clamps motor duty cycle to zero.

---

## The Accumulating Design Dossier: Exiting Part I

Upon completing Part I, the engineering team locks the first three foundational artifacts of the **Cumulative Design Dossier**:

1. `LOOP-01` (**Loop Charter**): Explicitly bounds physical authority, defines maximum permissible kinetic energy ($E_{\text{max}}$), and establishes the Proposal–Permission boundary.
2. `REQ-01` (**Requirements & Assumptions Ledger**): Establishes the hard timing deadline budget ($t_{\text{total}} \le t_{\text{deadline}}$), information age limits ($\Delta t_{\text{max}}$), and tail-latency ceilings ($P_{99} \le 45\text{ ms}$).
3. `RUN-01` (**Runtime Skeleton**): Freezes the lock-free shared memory layout, atomic sequence counter contracts, and watchdog lease timeouts ($\tau_{\text{watchdog}} = 50\text{ ms}$).
